title: Woman arrested in Philadelphia after blocking delivery robot in ongoing sidewalk protest

tea.why: A Philadelphia woman is protesting against delivery robots over concerns regarding job losses for delivery workers, sidewalk safety, and privacy risks.
tea.want: To draw attention to corporate abuses in public spaces and exercise free speech against autonomous delivery machines.
tea.changed: Oct 31: The protester stated she plans to continue blocking and protesting the delivery robots despite receiving a disorderly conduct citation.

summary: A 78-year-old retired university professor in Philadelphia has been conducting an ongoing solo protest against autonomous delivery robots by standing in their path on public sidewalks. The actions, which she began months prior to draw attention to delivery worker job losses, sidewalk safety, and camera privacy risks, led to police intervention earlier in the month near the 1200 block of Filbert Street. According to the Philadelphia Police Department, officers responded to a criminal mischief report and issued a disorderly conduct citation after the protester allegedly ignored orders to move. The protester maintained her actions are protected free speech and expressed intent to continue her demonstrations.
demands: Stop the use of autonomous delivery robots on public sidewalks
Address sidewalk safety concerns regarding robots
Address privacy risks from cameras embedded in delivery machines
response: According to the Philadelphia Police Department, officers responded to the scene after receiving a report regarding a robot, and issued a disorderly conduct citation after the individual allegedly ignored repeated orders to move.

updates.text: The protester stated she intends to continue blocking delivery robots as protected free speech.
